messages:
Raj Patel: Heads-up — between 08:10 and 08:22 UTC we saw an eviction spike in asia-south1 (~28% spot GPUs). Fallback pool didn't absorb traffic; a bunch of pods stayed Pending.
Maria Chen: ugh. any reason fallback nodes didn't scale? autoscaler logs?
Oliver Wong: I pulled the CA logs — scale-up events were throttled by quota: 'couldn't create nodes: quotaExceeded'. Fallback pool is in a different node pool with a separate quota but it looks like the zone hit a regional GPU quota overall.
Raj Patel: right, fallback pool shares the regional GPU quota. We designed it that way to keep cost under control, but this means when region-wide evictions happen it's useless.
Samira K.: Suggestion: split fallback into multiple zonal nodepools (fallback-az1 / fallback-az2) + smaller per-pool quota so at least some AZs can come up. Also add a tiny on-demand buffer (2-4 nodes) per zone as hot standby.
Maria Chen: +1. Also we should rate-limit preemptible provisioning to avoid a thundering herd on control plane when reclaiming lots of pods.
Oliver Wong: note: control-plane quota is fine, it's the GPU SKU quota that's the limiter. We can request a quota bump but that's slow for some customers.
Raj Patel: short-term ops plan: 1) Add a 2-node on-demand hot-standby in each zone. 2) Split fallback into zonal pools with taints: 'node.kubernetes.io/fallback: true'. 3) Update routing to prefer fallback zonal pool rather than single regional pool.
Jen L.: Do we have a cost estimate for 2-node on-demand per zone? want to model impact.
Samira K.: rough calc: p4 on-demand ~ $3.2/hr (per node) in asia-south1, so 2 nodes x 3 zones x 24h ≈ $460/day. We can make them tiny (lower GPU) or use CPU-heavy small VMs and rely on evictable pods landing there with CPU-only fallback for limited work.
Maria Chen: alternative: keep 0 hot nodes but have an aggressive warm-prewarm rotation: rotate a small set of preemptible nodes across zones every 10 minutes so preemption risk is distributed.
Raj Patel: rotation helps resilience but doesn't solve quota exhaustion. If regional GPU quota gets eaten by other customers, rotation is moot.
Infra Bot: k8s-notify: pod disruptor detected 45 pod evictions in namespace production-inference between 08:10 and 08:22 UTC. Drains initiated on nodes gpu-preemptible-3a/3b.
Oliver Wong: Another failure mode: cluster autoscaler backoff kicks in after repeated scale failures — then it waits 5m, 10m, etc. We hit backoff and no new attempts were made while the wave continued.
Samira K.: We could customize CA's backoff policy per nodepool (shorter backoff for fallback pools) or write an operator that forces a hot-standby create when eviction rate > X.
Raj Patel: action items: A) Maria to draft config change for zonal fallback pools + taints + routing (due EOD). B) Oliver to file quota request and add monitoring alert for GPU quota saturation (low noise threshold) — due tomorrow. C) Samira to prototype rotation vs on-demand cost tradeoffs — quick doc by Wednesday.
Maria Chen: I'll also add a policy to set CA max-unready-nodes-percentage lower for GPU pools so we don't over-evict scheduling capacity.
Jen L.: For customers on Dedicated we should expose a flag whether fallback uses shared regional quota or isolated reserved quota — that will be a selling point.
Oliver Wong: One more: add a probe that detects CA backoff state and triggers a mitigation runbook (e.g., create single on-demand node, or bump nodepool size temporarily). It can be a simple controller.
Raj Patel: Thanks all. If anyone sees the same pattern in other regions please ping here. I'll kick off a short playbook with rollback steps.
Samira K.: FYI I'll run a chaos sim for 30m tomorrow at 09:00 UTC to validate rotation + fallback. Expect brief alerts.
Maria Chen: noted. tagging @oncall for awareness.
Infra Bot: deploy-bot: created change request cr-4821 for 'zonal-fallback-nodepools' with roll strategy canary (1 zone).
